01 / THE METHOD

An agent that knows
what comes next.

Motor commands alone do not describe progress. LAW gives planning, action generation, and evaluation a common objective: the active semantic subtask.

01

Plan

Predict the remaining semantic subtasks.

02

Propose

Generate 32 diverse action chunks.

03

Select

Score candidates and fuse the top eight.

04

Execute

Execute a prefix of the fused action.

05

Monitor

Assess completion asynchronously; continue or advance.

A

Shared dynamics.
Specialized experts.

MoTE places shared and modality-specific experts after joint video–action attention. Shared computation captures common physical structure, while private experts preserve each modality’s distinct features.

B

Persistent context.
At the right detail.

RecentBoundaryLong-term

Recent observations and subtask-boundary states retain spatial detail. Older history is compressed. The VLM and WAM use aligned timestamps in their own native token spaces.

C

Useful supervision.
Even from failed episodes.

Subtask-local value learning preserves credit for completed stages. A successful subtask receives terminal reward 1; returns stop at semantic boundaries rather than inheriting the outcome of the entire episode.

04 / SEMANTIC PROGRESS

Long tasks.
Meaningful steps.

Subtasks connect language to physical changes: open a drawer, place a block, close the drawer. The same progress representation spans simulated and real environments.

Semantic boundaries and subtask descriptions in RoboTwin demonstrations.

RoboDojo additionally examines generalization, precision, long-horizon behavior, memory, and open skills. The manuscript discusses these complementary capability dimensions.

THE RESEARCH

Language, action,
and a persistent world.

Long-horizon robot tasks require more than accurate motor commands: an agent must plan meaningful subtasks, recognize when they are complete, and select actions that advance the current objective.

LAW coordinates a hybrid-expert vision-language model with a world-action model through semantic subtask progress. Specialized planner, state, and value experts share a frozen VLM backbone. MoTE strengthens joint video–action modeling, while dual-stream hierarchical memory retains recent observations, semantic boundary states, and compressed history. Subtask-local value learning preserves useful supervision from successful stages of failed trajectories.

The resulting framework achieves 94.21% average success on 50 RoboTwin tasks, rising to 95.56% with an OpenWAM-α backbone, and 65% average success on three long-horizon real-robot tasks.
